target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (X Y : Type), Nonempty X → ∀ (Q : S1 X Y → Prop),
    (∀ N, N.D11 → Q N) → (∃ N, ¬ Q N) →
    ∀ c4 : (List X → Y) → Prop,
      ∃ N : S1 X Y, ¬ (Q N ↔ c4 N.d4)
a_raw: {"translation": "Target defines (names, without asserting or proving) a proposition about systems of type S1 X Y. A system N of type S1 X Y consists of: a finite type A1 of components (with a Fintype instance); for each component n in A1, a state type A3 n (not required to be finite); an initial global state a4 assigning to each n in A1 an element of A3 n; an update function a5 taking a component n in A1, a global state σ : (m : A1) → A3 m, and an input x in X to a new state in A3 n; and an output function a6 mapping a global state to a value in Y. Given such a system N, its input-output function N.d4 : List X → Y maps a finite list xs of elements of X to the output obtained by starting at the initial global state N.a4, folding left to right over xs using the synchronous one-step update (σ, x) ↦ (fun n => N.a5 n σ x), and applying N.a6 to the final global state. Define a directed dependence step N.D8 m n between components m, n in N.A1 to hold when there exist two global states σ, σ' : (k : N.A1) → N.A3 k (not restricted to reachable states) and an input x in X such that σ k = σ' k for all k ≠ m, while N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x (that is, changing only component m can change the next state of component n for some input). The condition N.D11 holds when N.A1 is nonempty and, for every pair m, n in N.A1 (including m = n), there is a nonempty finite chain of N.D8 steps from m to n of length at least 1 (zero steps do not count, so every component must also lie on a directed cycle of length at least 1). With these definitions, Target is the proposition that: for all types X and Y, assuming X is nonempty, for every predicate Q : S1 X Y → Prop, assuming (1) Q N holds for every N : S1 X Y satisfying N.D11 and (2) there exists at least one N : S1 X Y for which Q N fails, then for every predicate c4 : (List X → Y) → Prop on input-output functions, there exists a system N : S1 X Y (which may depend on X, Y, Q, and c4) such that Q N is not logically equivalent to c4 (N.d4) (i.e., ¬ (Q N ↔ c4 N.d4)). No finiteness, computability, or regularity conditions are imposed on X, Y, A3 n, Q, or c4, and no explicit nonemptiness or cardinality hypothesis is placed on Y (though the hypothesis that some N : S1 X Y satisfies ¬ Q N implicitly requires S1 X Y, and hence Y via N.a6 N.a4, to be nonempty)."}
translation: Target defines (names, without asserting or proving) a proposition about systems of type S1 X Y. A system N of type S1 X Y consists of: a finite type A1 of components (with a Fintype instance); for each component n in A1, a state type A3 n (not required to be finite); an initial global state a4 assigning to each n in A1 an element of A3 n; an update function a5 taking a component n in A1, a global state σ : (m : A1) → A3 m, and an input x in X to a new state in A3 n; and an output function a6 mapping a global state to a value in Y. Given such a system N, its input-output function N.d4 : List X → Y maps a finite list xs of elements of X to the output obtained by starting at the initial global state N.a4, folding left to right over xs using the synchronous one-step update (σ, x) ↦ (fun n => N.a5 n σ x), and applying N.a6 to the final global state. Define a directed dependence step N.D8 m n between components m, n in N.A1 to hold when there exist two global states σ, σ' : (k : N.A1) → N.A3 k (not restricted to reachable states) and an input x in X such that σ k = σ' k for all k ≠ m, while N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x (that is, changing only component m can change the next state of component n for some input). The condition N.D11 holds when N.A1 is nonempty and, for every pair m, n in N.A1 (including m = n), there is a nonempty finite chain of N.D8 steps from m to n of length at least 1 (zero steps do not count, so every component must also lie on a directed cycle of length at least 1). With these definitions, Target is the proposition that: for all types X and Y, assuming X is nonempty, for every predicate Q : S1 X Y → Prop, assuming (1) Q N holds for every N : S1 X Y satisfying N.D11 and (2) there exists at least one N : S1 X Y for which Q N fails, then for every predicate c4 : (List X → Y) → Prop on input-output functions, there exists a system N : S1 X Y (which may depend on X, Y, Q, and c4) such that Q N is not logically equivalent to c4 (N.d4) (i.e., ¬ (Q N ↔ c4 N.d4)). No finiteness, computability, or regularity conditions are imposed on X, Y, A3 n, Q, or c4, and no explicit nonemptiness or cardinality hypothesis is placed on Y (though the hypothesis that some N : S1 X Y satisfies ¬ Q N implicitly requires S1 X Y, and hence Y via N.a6 N.a4, to be nonempty).

divergences.description: Stand-in D11 vs. numerical ϕ and 'arbitrarily high ϕ': although the author declares 'integrated' (D11) as a stand-in rather than IIT's ϕ, D11 is a fixed binary graph property (nonempty, strongly connected with a directed cycle through every node, checking causal dependence over all global states including unreachable ones). Unlike [P-D52b] and [P-D57], which construct systems with arbitrarily high ϕ (defeating theories with any positive ϕ-threshold), Target cannot express graded or arbitrarily high integration; moreover, because D11 is satisfied even by single-node self-looping systems (A1 = Unit), the hypothesis (∀ N, N.D11 → Q N) excludes verdicts Q that require multi-component (≥ 2 nodes) integration or a threshold above minimal integration.

Existential disagreement vs. universal per-system equivalence: [P-D52b] and [P-D57] state universally that for every feedforward system (and every input-output function, or 'each system that provides evidence for IIT') there exists a functionally equivalent recurrent/high-ϕ system. Target only states that every input-output inference c4 disagrees with Q on at least one system (∃ N), matching the author's narrower claim rather than the full universal statement.

Weakened non-consciousness premise: whereas [P-D52b] and [P-D53] assume that feedforward (ϕ = 0) systems are not conscious, Target only requires that some system is not conscious (∃ N, ¬ Q N), without requiring that system to be feedforward (D9). Since feedforward systems exist whenever Y is nonempty, this is a harmless strengthening of the theorem.

Idealizations of the system model and empirical inference: S1 X Y models systems as deterministic, discrete-time, synchronous finite-component machines with a fixed initial state and unrestricted (possibly infinite) per-node state types A3 n (which even allows an arbitrary system's state to be packed into a single node). Consciousness Q and empirical inference c4 are idealized as binary Prop predicates rather than graded measures or finite physical/probabilistic experiments, though giving c4 the entire unbounded input-output map List X → Y strengthens the impossibility result relative to finite experiments.

Explicit Nonempty X hypothesis (declared): Target explicitly assumes at least one input exists, which the source leaves implicit (e.g., x → F(x) in [P-D57]). In Lean this is technically necessary because D7 quantifies existentially over x : X, so without Nonempty X the predicate D11 would be vacuously false and Target would fail.

judgement.summary: Target faithfully captures the logical structure of the converse unfolding argument as claimed—showing that under a verdict where integrated causal structure is sufficient for consciousness and some system is non-conscious, no predicate of the full unbounded input-output map agrees with the verdict everywhere. The main caveats are minor and largely stem from declared idealizations, notably that the binary stand-in D11 includes single-node self-looping systems and cannot express the source's 'arbitrarily high ϕ' strengthening, and that Target concludes existential disagreement on some system rather than the source's universal per-system equivalence.
